A curve in a level road has a radius \( 75 \mathrm{~m} \). The maximum speed of a car turning this curved road can be \( 30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \) without skidding. [JEE Main 2022, 25 June (Shift 2)]

Condition for no skidding,

fs(max)=mv2rf_{s(\max)} = \frac{mv^2}{r}

Also static friction, fs(max)=μmg

⇒μmg=mv2r\Rightarrow \mu mg = \frac{mv^2}{r}
⇒v=μgr\Rightarrow v = \sqrt{\mu gr}

Since the coefficient of friction remains the same,

⇒30:v2=75:48=25:16=5:4\Rightarrow 30 : v_2 = \sqrt{75} : \sqrt{48} = \sqrt{25} : \sqrt{16} = 5 : 4
⇒v2=24 m/s\Rightarrow v_2 = 24 \text{ m/s}

When the height of the water level is \(10 \mathrm{~cm}\), the rate (in \(\mathrm{cm}^2 / \mathrm{sec}\) ) at which the wet conical surface area of the vessel increases is

 

[JEE Main 2022, 25 June (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let the height of water be \(h\) cm and the radius of its upper surface be \(r\) cm.

The complete vessel has height \(35\) cm and radius \(7\) cm.

By similarity of cones,

\(\dfrac rh=\dfrac7{35}=\dfrac15\).

Therefore, \(r=\dfrac h5\).

The slant height of the water cone is \(l=\sqrt{h^2+r^2}\).

Substituting \(r=\dfrac h5\),

we get \(l=\sqrt{h^2+\dfrac{h^2}{25}}\).

Thus \(l=\sqrt{\dfrac{26h^2}{25}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{26}}5h\).

The volume of water is \(V=\dfrac13\pi r^2h\).

Hence \(V=\dfrac13\pi\left(\dfrac h5\right)^2h=\dfrac{\pi h^3}{75}\).

Differentiate with respect to time.

We get \(\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{3\pi h^2}{75}\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{\pi h^2}{25}\dfrac{dh}{dt}\).

Given \(\dfrac{dV}{dt}=1\,\mathrm{cm^3/sec}\) and \(h=10\) cm,

we obtain \(1=\dfrac{\pi(10)^2}{25}\dfrac{dh}{dt}\).

Therefore, \(1=4\pi\dfrac{dh}{dt}\).

Hence \(\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac1{4\pi}\,\mathrm{cm/sec}\).

The wet curved surface area is \(A=\pi rl\).

Substituting \(r=\dfrac h5\) and \(l=\dfrac{\sqrt{26}}5h\),

we get \(A=\dfrac{\pi\sqrt{26}}{25}h^2\).

Differentiate with respect to time.

Thus \(\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{2\pi\sqrt{26}}{25}h\dfrac{dh}{dt}\).

At \(h=10\), we get

\(\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{2\pi\sqrt{26}}{25}(10)\left(\dfrac1{4\pi}\right)\).

Simplifying gives \(\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{\sqrt{26}}5\,\mathrm{cm^2/sec}\).

Let \( f(x)=\left|(x-1)\left(x^{2}-2 x-3\right)\right|+x-3, x \in R \). If \( m \) and \( M \) are respectively the number of points of local minimum and local maximum of \( f \) in the interval \( (0,4) \), then \( m+M \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 25 June (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(p(x)=(x-1)(x^2-2x-3)=(x-1)(x-3)(x+1)\)

For \(0<x<1\), \(p(x)>0\),

so \(f(x)=p(x)+x-3=x^3-3x^2\)

Then \(f'(x)=3x(x-2)<0\),

so \(f\) decreases on \((0,1)\)

For \(1<x<3\), \(p(x)<0\),

so \(f(x)=-p(x)+x-3=-x^3+3x^2+2x-6\)

Then \(f'(x)=-3x^2+6x+2\)

The equation \(f'(x)=0\) gives \(x=1\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{15}}{3}\)

Only \(x=1+\dfrac{\sqrt{15}}{3}\) lies in \((1,3)\)

The derivative changes from positive to negative there,

so this point is a local maximum.

At \(x=1\), the function decreases on the left and increases on the right,

so \(x=1\) is a local minimum.

For \(3<x<4\), \(p(x)>0\),

so \(f(x)=p(x)+x-3=x^3-3x^2\)

Then \(f'(x)=3x(x-2)>0\),

so \(f\) increases on \((3,4)\)

At \(x=3\), the function decreases on the left and increases on the right,

so \(x=3\) is a local minimum.

Therefore, the number of local minima is \(m=2\)

and the number of local maxima is \(M=1\)

Hence \(m+M=2+1=3\).

questions.question:
If the mean deviation about the mean of the numbers \( 1,2,3, \ldots, n \), where \( n \) is  odd, is \( \frac{5(n+1)}{n} \), then \( n \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 25 June (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(n=2m+1\), because \(n\) is odd.

The mean of the first \(n\) positive integers is

\(\displaystyle \overline x=\dfrac{n+1}{2}=m+1\)

The sum of the absolute deviations from the mean is

\(\displaystyle 2\sum_{j=1}^{m}j=m(m+1)\)

The mean deviation about the mean is

\(\displaystyle \dfrac{m(m+1)}{n}=\dfrac{(n-1)(n+1)}{4n}=\dfrac{n^2-1}{4n}\)

The given condition is

\(\displaystyle \dfrac{n^2-1}{4n}=\dfrac{5(n+1)}{n}\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow n^2-1=20(n+1)\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow (n-1)(n+1)=20(n+1)\)

\(\because n+1>0\),

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow n-1=20\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow n=21\)

The required value is \(21\).
